law: A step's per-unit deadline check reads the real clock about once per target interval instead of once per unit and overshoots its deadline by at most one read interval. A step begins at its driver's entry reading, so the first in-step call costs no read and the calibrated stride carries from step to step; outside the job's own strided reads a worker step reads the clock exactly twice, on entry and on exit, and every trace event and next-step decision reuses those readings.
